source.title: The origin and evolution of transition discs: successes, problems and open questions

accepted.question_text: Are the objects called pre-transition discs—discs that otherwise resemble transition discs but retain either a small amount of optically thin inner dust or a radially thin optically thick inner wall near the dust-destruction front—actually evolutionary precursors of transition discs, and is there any evolutionary path connecting them to transition discs that show only photospheric emission out to the mid-infrared?

evidence.quote: Espaillat et al. (2010) labelled these discs as "Pre-transition discs", such that the small amount of inner dust could represent the final stages of its disappearance.

To date there is no evidence that these discs are precursors to transition discs or that there is an evolutionary path that connects these discs to transition discs that show only photospheric emission out to the MIR.

accepted.question_text: When a Weak-lined T-Tauri star shows an infrared excess but little or no gas emission, should that object be classified as a transition disc in the last stage of its protoplanetary lifetime or instead as a young debris disc whose dust is secondary and collisionally regenerated?

evidence.quote: Obviously, this could give rise to confusion into how to classify a WTTs with an infra-red excess: is it a transition disc at the end of its life or a young debris disc?
Therefore, Hardy et al. (2015) concluded that the majority of WTTs with infra-red excesses were in-fact young debris discs rather than evolved transition discs.

accepted.question_text: For the low-mm-flux, small-hole transition-disc population that is probably undergoing true disc dispersal, what are the actual gas and dust structures inside the inferred cavities: do the spectral-energy-distribution-inferred holes exist when imaged directly, is there any non-axisymmetric structure, and how much gas remains inside those cavities?

evidence.quote: In most cases all the information in hole size and dust distribution come from photometry and SED fitting.
Additionally, given the hole sizes are small and mm fluxes are low, no imaging campaign has confirmed the presence of the holes inferred from the SED or probed any non-axisymmteric structure.
Since these discs are likely to actually be discs in transition, more observations are required to constrain the structures in both gas and dust of these discs.

accepted.question_text: In mm-bright transition discs, are most of the small dust particles removed at roughly the same radius as the trapped mm-sized particles, or do the small grains extend much farther inward while only the larger grains remain confined to the outer ring?

evidence.quote: However, there are still a few outstanding issues, particularly with regard to the structure and kinematics of the gas component and the distribution of small dust particles in the outer disc.

For example: are the bulk of the small dust particles removed at a location similar to the mm-sized dust particles or do they extend much further in as hinted at by SEEDs images of the surfaces of the discs?

accepted.question_text: What is the true gas structure and kinematics inside mm-bright transition-disc cavities, and how should the currently observed gas density drops and inner-cavity gas detections be reconciled into a single physical picture?

evidence.quote: It is not clear how this fits into the entire picture yet as gas has only been imaged in a few cases and the interpretation is not without problems as we will discuss in Section-4.
However, there are still a few outstanding issues, particularly with regard to the structure and kinematics of the gas component

accepted.question_text: Can photoevaporation, possibly aided by thermal sweeping or some other rapid outer-disc-clearing process, avoid producing a long-lived population of optically thick, non-accreting transition discs with large holes and thereby match the observed scarcity of such objects?

evidence.quote: Thus, the lack of observed optically thick non-accreting transition discs with large hole radii, points to an issue with the photoevaporation model.
As such, the lack of non-accreting transition discs from the photoevaporation model still remains an open problem and issue for the photoevaporation scenario.
The "thermal-sweeping" instability (Owen et al. 2013) may go a long way to resolving these issues; however, it is too early to say if it works efficiently enough to be consistent with the data.

accepted.question_text: If giant planets create mm-bright transition discs, what physical mechanism removes or traps enough 1–10 micron dust from the inner disc to suppress the near-infrared excess while still leaving a mm cavity, maintaining active accretion onto the star, and remaining consistent with scattered-light and thermal-infrared observations?

evidence.quote: Thus, dust filtration alone cannot remove small 1 − 10 µm dust particles.

This is problematic as small particles dominate the opacity, so if they indeed follow the gas through the gap and populate the inner disc then the disc will show a strong IR-excess at all wavelengths and have an SED consistent with a primordial disc.
One must find a model that produces a mm ring, scattered light image consistent with the SEEDs structure, a lack of NIR excess and active accretion.

accepted.question_text: Can grain growth inside or near a planet-opened gap, under realistic drift, fragmentation, and opacity constraints, convert enough small dust into larger particles quickly enough to explain transition-disc spectral-energy distributions without creating contradictory mm emission or replenishing the small-grain population?

evidence.quote: Whether all these conditions can be met in the wide observed range of parameter space still remains an open question.

Calculations by Pinilla, Benisty, & Birnstiel (2012b); Pinilla et al. (2015) have demonstrated that this could in principle work; however, since these particle may drift, grow and fragment on a time-scale comparable to the lifetimes of transition discs then how this removal mechanism causes the NIR colours and scattered light images to evolve in time is of crucial importance to asses whether grain growth can provide the answer.

accepted.question_text: If planets are responsible for mm-bright transition discs, how is the planetary-mobility problem avoided—either by preventing the gap-opening planet from migrating inward into the small-hole regime or by causing the transition-disc spectral signature to disappear before the system would overproduce accreting, high-mm-flux, small-hole discs that are not observed?

evidence.quote: This gave rise to a population of transition discs with small . 10 AU transition discs and comparable mm fluxes to mm-bright transition discs. There are very few transition discs observed with large mm-fluxes and small hole sizes.

The "planetary-mobility problem" discussed by Clarke & Owen (2013) indicated that planet would migrate into a forbidden region of planet space, giving rise to a transition disc with a high mm flux and small hole.

accepted.question_text: What mechanism replenishes the severely depleted inner gas discs of many transition discs quickly enough to sustain the observed stellar accretion rates, given that inferred inner-disc draining times can be tens to thousands of years and therefore are far shorter than standard viscous draining times?

evidence.quote: For some transition discs this exercise yields incredibly short draining time-scales
Clearly all most all these time-scales are incompatible with viscous draining which would point to a time-scale more like 106 years for hole radii of several 10s of AU.

However, a mechanism that can refill these inner disc cavities at such rapid time-scales. In the case of IRS 48 this resupply time-scale is worrying similar to the orbital time-scale at the cavity radius as it would require highly supersonic replenishment.

accepted.question_text: Do discs that retain a primordial-looking spectral energy distribution but show a large mm cavity constitute a hidden population physically associated with transition discs, and if so are they precursors to, contemporaries of, or descendants from the better-known transition-disc classes?

evidence.quote: Finally, we suggest that the few discs with primordial looking SEDs, but serendipitously imaged, showing large cavities in the mm (e.g. MWC758 & WSB 60) may represent a hidden population of associated objects.
Whether these are an isolated rare example or point to a large hidden population of discs with no NIR deficient and a mm hole is an intriguing question.

Characterising whether these disc are an a stage in the evolution of a transition disc: i.e. are they precursors or former transition discs would place further constraints on any transition disc models.

accepted.question_text: Are the non-axisymmetric structures now seen in many imaged transition discs genuinely special to transition discs, or are they common features of primordial protoplanetary discs as well and therefore not diagnostic of the transition-disc phenomenon by themselves?

evidence.quote: For example, are the non-axis symmetric structure we see in transition discs purely associated with this type of object or just a feature of all protoplanetary discs?
